_about: Public-domain Sylvanus Stall (1847-1915), Lutheran minister of Lancaster and Baltimore and publisher, for the Word Hoard: Five Minute Object Sermons to Children, Talks to the King's Children, With the Children on Sundays, the Ministers' Hand-Book to Lutheran Hymns, How to Pay Church Debts, Methods of Church Work, Bible Selections for Daily Devotion, and his Self and Sex books for men and boys (What a Young Boy, a Young Man, a Young Husband, and a Man of Forty-Five Ought to Know), and What Parents Should Teach their Children. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 113 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

stall-lutheran-hymns: Ministers' hand-book to Lutheran hymns, in the "Book of worship" (Easton, Pa. : Skinner & Finch, Printers, 1879)
stall-church-debts: How to pay church debts : and how to keep churches out of debt (New York : I. K. Funk, 1881)
stall-church-work: Methods of church work : religious, social and financial (New York : Funk & Wagnalls, 1887)
stall-object-sermons: Five minute object sermons to children : ... through eye-gate and ear-gate into the city of child-soul (New York : Funk & Wagnalls, 1894)
stall-bible-selections: Bible selections for daily devotion; 365 readings (New York, London [etc.] Funk & Wagnalls company, 1896)
stall-young-man: What a young man ought to know (Philadelphia ; London : Vir ; Toronto : W. Briggs, 1897)
stall-young-husband: What a young husband ought to know (Philadelphia ; London : Vir, 1897)
stall-forty-five: What a man of forty-five ought to know (Philadelphia : The Vir Publishing Company; [etc, etc., 1901)
stall-young-boy: What a Young Boy ought to Know (The Vir Publishing Company, 1905)
stall-children-sundays: With the Children on Sundays (The Uplift Publishing Company, 1911)
stall-parents: What parents should teach their children (Philadelphia, Boston [etc.] American Baptist publication society, 1912)

_excluded.stall-others: What a Young Girl Ought to Know is by Mary Wood-Allen; the Finnish and Armenian translations and his salesmen's manual are left out
